$why: Chosen by reading the transcriptions (transcripts/*/batch-*.fr.tex): passages in his own words with little or no mathematics, each checked against its batch and page. A selection, not a census; edit by hand. « weight » (3–5) is how striking the reader judged it; the page shows the heaviest first.

quotes.text: Au moment d'écrire ces lignes, et malgré l'assistance de gens compétents comme Katz, il ne semble pas qu'un résultat de cette nature soit prouvé, même […] pour des courbes planes […] de grand degré.
quotes.en: At the time of writing these lines, and despite the help of competent people like Katz, it seems that no result of this kind has been proved, even […] for plane curves […] of large degree.
quotes.context: Typescript on a heuristic count of Frobenius eigenvalues that are p-adic units, noting an open point-counting question.

quotes.text: Je vous avoue d'ailleurs que j'ai de grands doutes que les choses marchent aussi simplement que ça, i.e. que la cohomologie rigide-analytique à coefficients constants tout bêtes donne les « bons » nombres de Betti. […] Il reste plausible néanmoins, quoi qu'il en soit, que la topologie rigide-analytique aura son rôle à jouer dans ces questions.
quotes.en: I confess, moreover, that I have great doubts that things work as simply as that, i.e. that rigid-analytic cohomology with plain constant coefficients gives the “right” Betti numbers. […] It remains plausible nonetheless, whatever the case, that the rigid-analytic topology will have its part to play in these questions.
quotes.context: His typed letter to Deligne of December 1965 on p-adic cohomology.

quotes.text: Il faut dire que tout ça est bien éculé, et qu'on ne pourra dire des choses vraiment intéressantes et nouvelles qu'en faisant appel à la « vraie » cohomologie p-adique.
quotes.en: It must be said that all this is rather hackneyed, and that one will only be able to say really interesting and new things by calling on the “true” p-adic cohomology.
quotes.context: Close of the 1965 letter to Deligne on p-adic cohomology.

quotes.text: Commentaire terminologique : Un cristal possède deux propriétés caractéristiques : la rigidité, et la faculté de croitre, dans un voisinage approprié. Il y a des cristaux de toute espèce de substance : des cristaux de soude, de soufre, de modules, d'anneaux, de schémas relatifs etc.
quotes.en: Terminological comment: a crystal has two characteristic properties: rigidity, and the faculty of growing, in a suitable neighbourhood. There are crystals of every kind of substance: crystals of soda, of sulphur, of modules, of rings, of relative schemes, etc.
quotes.context: Opening of his typed and hand-corrected letter to Tate (Pisa, May 1966) introducing the notion of crystal.

quotes.text: J'ai réfléchi aux groupes formels et à la cohomologie de De Rahm, et suis arrivé à un projet de théorie, ou plutôt de début de théorie, que j'ai envie de t'exposer[,] pour me clarifier les idées.
quotes.en: I have been thinking about formal groups and De Rham cohomology, and have arrived at a project of a theory, or rather of the beginning of a theory, which I feel like explaining to you, to clarify my own ideas.
quotes.context: First sentence of the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals.

quotes.text: Un retour en arrière. La définition 1.1. et le sorite 1.3. sont un petit peu canulés. […] Il est probable qu'il y aura bien d'autres canulars de détail dans ces notes, mais[,] je pense[,] sans conséquence !
quotes.en: A step back. Definition 1.1 and sorite 1.3 are a little bit botched. […] There will probably be plenty of other small botches in these notes, but, I think, of no consequence!
quotes.context: In the letter to Tate he goes back to correct his own definition of crystals, which only works locally.

quotes.text: L'affirmation du titre n'est pour l'instant qu'une hypothèse ou un voeux pieux, mais je suis convaincu qu'elle est essentiellement correcte.
quotes.en: The claim in the title is for the moment only a hypothesis or a pious wish, but I am convinced that it is essentially correct.
quotes.context: Chapter 2 of the letter to Tate, on the conjecture that the De Rham cohomology of a variety in characteristic p is a crystal.

quotes.text: Deux grosses imperfections dans leur tapis : 1º ils n'obtiennent que des invariants cohomologiques locaux […] ; pour avoir un invariant global, ils doivent se limiter à la dimension 1. On peut penser que cela tient à leur manque de familiarité avec les machines cohomologiques.
quotes.en: Two big flaws in their carpet: 1) they only obtain local cohomological invariants […]; to get a global invariant they have to restrict to dimension 1. One may think this is due to their lack of familiarity with cohomological machinery.
quotes.context: His assessment, in the letter to Tate, of Washnitzer and Monsky's p-adic cohomology.

quotes.text: Je n'ai pas vérifié, à vrai dire, les deux affirmations, mais n'ai pas le moindre doute qu'elles sont correctes telles quelles.
quotes.en: I have not, to tell the truth, checked the two claims, but have not the slightest doubt that they are correct as they stand.
quotes.context: Letter to Tate, on describing the Dieudonné module of an abelian variety through its De Rham cohomology.

quotes.text: Mais je dois dire que ce drôle de comportement, où on aurait une stratification naturelle en car. p et une autre en car. 0, sans qu'elles veuillent se recoller, semble assez canularesque.
quotes.en: But I must say that this odd behaviour, where one would have a natural stratification in characteristic p and another in characteristic 0 which refuse to glue together, seems rather farcical.
quotes.context: Letter to Tate, on the De Rham cohomology of the family of elliptic curves near supersingular points.

quotes.text: Mais le « lecteur informé » […] notera à quel point une simple dualité de ce type est étriquée et pauvre.
quotes.en: But the “informed reader” […] will note how cramped and poor a mere duality of this kind is.
quotes.context: Notes for a 1966 talk on De Rham cohomology, wishing for a full six-operations duality formalism.

quotes.text: On peut évidemment se demander : pourquoi à tout prix […] nos programmes d'algébrisation et de généralisation à outrance de la cohomologie de De Rham. On dispose déjà des invariants cohomologiques ℓ-adiques […]
quotes.en: One may of course ask: why at all costs […] our programmes of algebraising and generalising De Rham cohomology to the utmost. We already have the ℓ-adic cohomological invariants […]
quotes.context: Opening of the survey of ℓ-adic theories in his 1966 talk notes, justifying the search for a p-adic cohomology.

quotes.text: On espère que Raynaud tirera au clair cette théorie, et ses analogues locaux — ce qui exigera d'ailleurs de surmonter des obstacles techniques considérables.
quotes.en: One hopes that Raynaud will clear up this theory, and its local analogues — which will, incidentally, require overcoming considerable technical obstacles.
quotes.context: 1966 talk notes, on flat cohomology as a route to p-adic invariants.

quotes.text: Comme conséquences, de ceci, sans doute, W.M. n'ont pas été capables de prouver pour leur cohomologie les propriétés formelles les plus élémentaires […]
quotes.en: As consequences of this, no doubt, W.M. have not been able to prove for their cohomology the most elementary formal properties […]
quotes.context: His critique of Washnitzer and Monsky's cohomology in the 1966 talk notes.

quotes.text: Il s'agit donc pour le moment d'une relation heuristique et sentimentale, entre deux idées différentes, dont les relations exactes laissent encore d'avoir été bien élucidées…… Pour résumer, on se trouve conduit devant un puzzle, où il s'agit de reconstituer une théorie d'ensemble […]
quotes.en: So for the moment this is a heuristic and sentimental relation between two different ideas, whose exact relations have yet to be properly elucidated…… To sum up, we are led to a puzzle, in which a whole theory has to be pieced together […]
quotes.context: 1966 talk notes, linking Washnitzer–Monsky invariance with the Gauss–Manin connection before introducing crystalline sites.

quotes.text: Ceci est un exercice plaisant et délectable, qui devrait figurer dans un travail systématique sur les ⊗-catégories, dans le chapitre des exemples.
quotes.en: This is a pleasant and delectable exercise, which ought to appear in a systematic work on ⊗-categories, in the chapter of examples.
quotes.context: His typescript for Saavedra, « Quelques exemples de catégories tensorielles », on when Hodge pre-structures are genuine Hodge structures.

quotes.text: N.B. On n'a aucune idée sur ce que pourrait être l'image essentielle du foncteur précédent, par exemple s'il y a lieu d'espérer qu'on trouve toutes les structures de Hodge […] ; cela semble peu probable, mais on n'a aucune indication sérieuse dans un sens ou l'autre.
quotes.en: N.B. One has no idea what the essential image of the preceding functor might be, for example whether one may hope to get all Hodge structures […]; that seems unlikely, but one has no serious indication either way.
quotes.context: Same typescript, on the functor from motives over the complex numbers to Hodge structures.

quotes.text: On respire ! Mais on fera attention que les foncteurs […] en question ne sont pas des foncteurs fibres proprement, mais des foncteurs fibres tordus. (On ne pourra s'empêcher de les appeler quand-même foncteurs fibres !)
quotes.en: We can breathe again! But one should take care that the functors […] in question are not fibre functors properly speaking, but twisted fibre functors. (One will not be able to help calling them fibre functors all the same!)
quotes.context: His typescript on ⊗-categories, after seeing that his result applies to semi-simple motives because the Künneth components are algebraic.

quotes.text: […] (ou multigradué ? Mais où s'arrêter ?). Le plus beau serait évidemment de trouver un théorème de structure général, sans supposer l'existence d'un foncteur fibre plus ou moins tordu où que ce soit […]
quotes.en: […] (or multigraded? But where to stop?). The finest thing would of course be to find a general structure theorem, without assuming the existence of a more or less twisted fibre functor anywhere at all […]
quotes.context: Same typescript on ⊗-categories, looking for intrinsic structure theorems in terms of gerbes.

quotes.text: On trouve un anneau bivariant jaugé simplicial, qui n'a plus aucune tendance à être spécial, et dont les composantes n'ont pas trop envie d'être de Poincaré ...
quotes.en: One finds a gauged bivariant simplicial ring which no longer has any tendency to be special, and whose components are not too keen on being Poincaré ...
quotes.context: Notes on bivariant graded algebras attached to varieties, taking Chow rings and cycles modulo equivalence instead of cohomology.

quotes.text: Bien entendu, la portée des « résultats » de notre travail est nécessairement sujette à caution, puisqu'ils dépendent de conjectures non prouvées à l'heure actuelle, savoir les conjectures de Weil et la résolution des singularités […]
quotes.en: Of course, the scope of the « results » of our work is necessarily open to question, since they depend on conjectures unproved at present, namely the Weil conjectures and resolution of singularities […]
quotes.context: Same typescript on weights and levels, where « sujette à caution » is his own hand's correction of « limitée ».

quotes.text: Par expérience personnelle, nous pensons cependant que la compréhension, obtenue grâce aux arguments de poids et de niveaux, quoiqu'elle soit pour l'instant entièrement heuristique, peut être la source de la découverte de propriétés importantes et inattendues pour la cohomologie des variétés algébriques, et qu'elle mérite pour cette raison de ne pas être dédaignée.
quotes.en: From personal experience, we nevertheless think that the understanding obtained through arguments of weight and level, although entirely heuristic for the moment, can be the source of the discovery of important and unexpected properties of the cohomology of algebraic varieties, and that it deserves for that reason not to be disdained.
quotes.context: Introduction to his own typescript on weights and levels in cohomology, corrected in his hand, defending conjectural heuristics.

quotes.text: […] le récent et magnifique travail de P. DELIGNE sur la théorie de Hodge généralisée des variétés algébriques quelconques […], justifie dès maintenant par voie transcendante le « yoga » des poids et niveaux dans le cadre de la cohomologie de De Rham (tout en ouvrant à la théorie cohomologique en caractéristique nulle des voies entièrement nouvelles).
quotes.en: […] the recent and magnificent work of P. Deligne on the generalised Hodge theory of arbitrary algebraic varieties […] already justifies, by transcendental means, the « yoga » of weights and levels in the setting of De Rham cohomology (while opening entirely new paths to cohomology theory in characteristic zero).
quotes.context: Same typescript introduction on weights, greeting Deligne's mixed Hodge theory as confirmation of his yoga.

quotes.text: I have become aware that I have been a bit rash with the conjectures I told you about Hodge structures, as in the form I stated them they contradict Tate's conjecture […]
quotes.context: Opening of a letter to Mumford, Algiers, 1 November 1965, retracting conjectures on families of Hodge structures.

quotes.text: So I really do not know what to believe!
quotes.context: Postscript of the 1965 letter to Mumford, after finding that the motive yoga and Tate's conjectures pull in opposite directions.

quotes.text: By the way, the fact that […] for a surface are algebraic was pointed out (Tate tells me) by Hodge […]. It is rather striking that this statement should not have struck the algebraic geometers more, and has fallen into oblivion for nearly thirty years !
quotes.context: Carbon copy of a typed letter of his to John Coates about the notes on the standard conjectures.

quotes.text: (The complete yoga then being that we have the category of motives which is semi-simple !). Without speeking of motives, and staying down on earth, it would be nice to explain in the notes that […]
quotes.context: Same letter to Coates, suggesting what to add to the written account of the standard conjectures.

quotes.text: Pour qu'il n'y ait pas de jaloux, il faudrait aussi répéter (i). Dans le présent paragraphe, ce sera sous cette forme que nous utiliserons 2.1. (mais il aurait été canularesque d'énoncer 2.1. avec des foncteurs contravariants).
quotes.en: So that nobody feels jealous, (i) ought to be repeated too. In this section it is in this form that we shall use 2.1 (but it would have been farcical to state 2.1 with contravariant functors).
quotes.context: His own carbon typescript on generalities about certain functors of modules.

quotes.text: La rédaction commence à faire un peu touffu, j'espère que tu pourras la rendre plus lisible. D'ailleurs, je me repens un peu de la définition 3.7. telle quelle […]
quotes.en: The write-up is starting to get a bit dense; I hope you can make it more readable. Besides, I somewhat repent of definition 3.7 as it stands […]
quotes.context: Annotated EGA IV typescript on Cohen algebras, addressed to its redactor.

quotes.text: À force de dévissage et de généralité, cette substance n'apparait pas assez clairement […]. Aussi le présent numéro rendra peut-être plus service si on commence à énoncer simplement 3.13. en théorème, […] et qu'on les démontre simultanément en deux pages ou trois, en laissant de côté tout le fatras anneaux admissibles, algèbres de Cohen etc. […] et un point c'est tout.
quotes.en: By dint of dévissage and generality, this substance does not come out clearly enough […]. So the present section will perhaps be more useful if one begins by simply stating 3.13 as a theorem, […] and proves them together in two or three pages, leaving aside all the clutter of admissible rings, Cohen algebras etc. […] and that's all.
quotes.context: Annotated typescript for EGA IV, addressed to its redactor, judging its own section too heavy and proposing to cut it down.

quotes.text: S'il en est bien ainsi, il s'imposera alors, pour les suites également, de réserver le mot le plus court à la notion qui manifestement est la plus serviable, et il faudra envisaher de changer notre terminologie […], en réservant tout au plus un terme tel que « suite strictement régulière » à la notion éculée. Bien sûr, dans le cas noethérien, les trois variantes (régulière, quasi, et Koko) sont équivalentes.
quotes.en: If that is indeed so, it will then be necessary, for sequences too, to reserve the shortest word for the notion that is plainly the most serviceable, and we shall have to consider changing our terminology […], keeping at most a term like 'strictly regular sequence' for the worn-out notion. Of course, in the noetherian case the three variants (regular, quasi, and Koko) are equivalent.
quotes.context: Typed postscript on why the definition of regular immersion in EGA IV fails outside the noetherian case and what to call things instead.

quotes.text: Du point de vue pratique, il me semble évidemment trop tard pour faire les changements désirables sur épreuves dans IV 16, 19. On peut cependant ajouter une remarque 19.1.8., dans laquelle nous ferions l'aveu que la définition adoptée dans le texte de immersion régulière s'est avérée peu maniable dans le cas non noethérien […]
quotes.en: From the practical point of view it seems obviously too late to make the desirable changes on the proofs of IV 16, 19. We can however add a remark 19.1.8, in which we would confess that the definition of regular immersion adopted in the text has turned out to be unwieldy in the non-noetherian case […]
quotes.context: Same postscript: how to own up in print to a definition in EGA IV that did not work.

quotes.text: I see you wrote them with much care, and I am all the more sorry that by my own fault, there is a number of misstatements which, I am affraid, will force you to do a serious recasting of the whole exposition. My notes definitely where too sketchy, and my oral explanations, I am affraid, partly wrong, which induced you into error a few times.
quotes.context: Opening of his reply to Murre after reading Murre's write-up of the tame fundamental group.

quotes.text: I hope that the theory will come out more clearly and correctly by devoting some care to generalities on ramification data (not necessarily of Kummer type). I will try to write something up within the next days. Please excuse me for the trouble I caused you by not learning my lesson well enough before I put you to work!
quotes.context: Letter to Murre listing the misstatements in the tame fundamental group exposé that he traces to his own notes.

quotes.text: Mais alors il semble qu'on soit infailliblement conduit à prendre comme catégorie […] la catégorie […] elle-même qu'on se propose de construire et d'étudier ! (Comparer avec la situation analogue pour les relations entre sites et topos, l'objet auxiliaire étant le site, l'objet intrinsèque de nature géométrique étant le topos associé à ce site).
quotes.en: But then it seems one is infallibly led to take as the category […] the very category […] one set out to construct and study! (Compare the analogous situation for the relations between sites and topoi, the auxiliary object being the site, the intrinsic object of geometric nature being the topos attached to that site.)
quotes.context: Typescript sketch on ramification data: what happens if one tries to remove the arbitrary choice in the auxiliary data.

quotes.text: Seule une rédaction en forme permettra de se rendre compte s'il y a lieu d'introduire cette notion d'image inverse, ou s'il ne vaut pas mieux donner des conditions axiomatiques […]. Ce sera sans doute le parti le plus raisonnable.
quotes.en: Only a proper write-up will show whether this notion of inverse image should be introduced, or whether it is better to give axiomatic conditions […]. That will no doubt be the most reasonable course.
quotes.context: Sketch on ramification data, on how to handle base change of the data.

quotes.text: This phenomenon explains why I have been so reluctant (wrongly so) to define tamely ramified coverings except in the Galois case […]. This shows rather clearly that even in the Galois case, the consideration of the category […] is undispensable for a good comprehension of what is really going on.
quotes.context: Typescript on ramification data, switching into English mid-page to explain to Murre why the category, not the covering, is the right object.

quotes.text: […] which has the disadvantage of being somewhat involved and artificial in its technical details, but has the merit of allowing explicit construction of the functor « geometric realization ». Otherwise, the set up outlined before the examples seems more natural, and giving a closer grasp of the really essential features of what « ramification data » should really mean.
quotes.context: Letter to Murre weighing an explicit but artificial example against a more natural general set-up.

quotes.text: I realize that all the indications I have given you so far are extremely sketshy, and as a consequence that I am charging you with a considerable amount of work to put some sense and order into all that. Thus it is I, not you, who should apologize for causing a lot of trouble ! […] As I am having some russian and chinese lessons on fridays, I will probably drop by on June 2.
quotes.context: Close of his 1967 covering letter to Murre, who was writing up the tame fundamental group for SGA 1 and had said he could not follow the new set-up.

quotes.text: Je vais prouver la conjecture du nº 6 pour des pinceaux de Lefschetz assez généraux d'hypersurfaces de grand degré, en adaptant la méthode utilisée par Katz pour les intersections complètes. [En marge, à l'encre, face à « vais prouver » entouré :] non, pas tout à fait !
quotes.en: I am going to prove the conjecture of no. 6 for sufficiently general Lefschetz pencils of hypersurfaces of large degree, adapting the method Katz used for complete intersections. [In the margin, in ink, against the circled 'am going to prove':] no, not quite!
quotes.context: Second draft of section 7 of the same typescript, with his later ink correction of his own announcement.

quotes.text: Nous avons utilisé le langage des motifs par pure commodité pour l'énoncé de 7.3. Comme ce langage n'est pas justifié à l'heure actuelle, il est préférable, pour le moment, de l'énoncer en termes de la filtration par le niveau sur la cohomologie ℓ-adique […]. Ceci dit, l'énoncé 7.3 […] est démontré sans aucune conjecture (pas même Lefschetz vache pour X …).
quotes.en: We used the language of motives purely for convenience in stating 7.3. As that language is not justified at present, it is better, for the moment, to state it in terms of the filtration by level on ℓ-adic cohomology […]. That said, statement 7.3 […] is proved without any conjecture (not even the nasty Lefschetz for X …).
quotes.context: Remark in his unpublished typescript on Griffiths' theorem by algebraic means, prepared around SGA 7.

quotes.text: La démonstration de 7.8 est par l'âne qui trotte […]
quotes.en: The proof of 7.8 is by the trotting donkey […]
quotes.context: Typescript on Griffiths' theorem: a proof dismissed as routine plodding.

quotes.text: Il est très confusant de faire semblant de traiter en même temps la carc. ≠ 2 et la car. 2. Pour l'instant, même les structures qui entrent en jeu sont d'espèce différente, et le traitement des deux cas est vraiment différent. Si donc tu n'arrives pas à une théorie commune satisfaisante, laisse tomber la car. 2, ou mets dans un numéro à part ce que tu sais en dire.
quotes.en: It is very confusing to pretend to treat characteristic ≠ 2 and characteristic 2 at the same time. For now even the structures involved are of a different kind, and the treatment of the two cases really is different. So if you do not reach a satisfactory common theory, drop characteristic 2, or put what you can say about it in a separate section.
quotes.context: His typed referee's letter of July 1961 commenting on a younger colleague's article on quadratic forms.

quotes.text: Une théorie vraiment satisfaisante devrait marcher sur tout préschéma S, et réciproquement. Je suis loin d'avoir des idées claires sur la question, et me borne à des remarques vagues:
quotes.en: A truly satisfactory theory should work over any prescheme S, and conversely. I am far from having clear ideas on the question, and confine myself to vague remarks:
quotes.context: Same 1961 referee's letter, on defining Stiefel–Whitney classes of quadratic forms independently of the characteristic.

quotes.text: (Il est évident que le contenu des exposés XI, XII, XV, XVI devrait être complètement refondu).
quotes.en: (It is obvious that the content of exposés XI, XII, XV, XVI ought to be completely recast.)
quotes.context: Marginal note in his hand on his own typescript of an SGA 3 exposé on maximal tori.

quotes.text: I must confess I did'nt look too thoroughly yet at the situation, and moreover I've been busy with rather different kind of things for the last two or three months, and lost a little contact. What is clear however is that the main key to an understanding of the general situation, is in an understanding of the basic particular case of Thurston's pants.
quotes.context: His 1984 letter to Lipman Bers about Teichmüller spaces and hyperbolic surfaces with boundary.

quotes.text: Il est étrange que l'icosaèdre, étudié depuis plus de deux mille ans dans des contextes et des optiques très divers, ne semble jamais avoir été étudié systématiquement du point de vue combinatoire […]. Ce « cours » se voudrait une investigation commune sur ce thème, en partant de l'intuition combinatoire la plus naïve, exemplifiée sur des modèles en carton (avec un coloriage convenable des arètes).
quotes.en: It is strange that the icosahedron, studied for more than two thousand years in very diverse contexts and perspectives, seems never to have been studied systematically from the combinatorial point of view […]. This “course” would like to be a joint investigation of this theme, starting from the most naive combinatorial intuition, illustrated on cardboard models (with a suitable colouring of the edges).
quotes.context: His typed announcement of the 1977-78 Montpellier course « Géométrie de l'icosaèdre ».

quotes.text: A partir d'un point de départ intuitif et familier, ce « cours » voudrait être une ouverture à un univers fascinant, pleins de mystères qui ne demandent qu'à être élucidés. Il ne peut donner des fruits qu'avec une participation active de l'étudiant et un travail personnel important […]
quotes.en: Starting from an intuitive and familiar point of departure, this “course” would like to be an opening onto a fascinating universe, full of mysteries only waiting to be elucidated. It can bear fruit only with the student's active participation and substantial personal work […]
quotes.context: His typed announcement of the 1977-78 DEA course on the arithmetic geometry of regular polygons.

quotes.text: Si le temps le permet et si d'autres investigations ne nous retiennent , nous tenterons, dans la volée, de construire l'icosaèdre régulier « général » sur un anneau de base convenable […]. (La caractéristique deux donnera sans doute du fil à retordre !).
quotes.en: If time allows and other investigations do not hold us back, we will try, in passing, to construct the “general” regular icosahedron over a suitable base ring […]. (Characteristic two will no doubt give us a hard time!)
quotes.context: Same 1977-78 DEA course announcement on regular polygons.

quotes.text: NB From my point of view, W is given beforehand in a rather tangible way, by a homological criterion, which turns out very handy. In Kan-Quillen's point of view, W was a little more hidden maybe […] Maybe I should have a look at Gabriel-Zisman and their treatment of « anodyne extensions ».
quotes.context: Notes on closed model structures and Quillen triples, contrasting his homological definition of weak equivalences with Kan and Quillen's.

quotes.text: Now this is about exactly the content of Quillen's version of « covering homotopy extension theorems » for simplicial closed model categories […] — although it was a little hard to make a sense of it, the way he stated it
quotes.context: Working notes on model categories, recognising a step as Quillen's covering homotopy extension theorem.

quotes.text: 132. A crazy tentative wrong-quadrant (bi)complex for the homotopy groups of a sphere.
quotes.context: His handwritten list of section titles for the end of Pursuing Stacks.

quotes.text: After a minute[']s thought, I feel very silly to find out that point a) is about trivial — that I have been dragging for months the notion of a total[ly] W-aspheric category A, without taking the trouble to sit down and look whether it really depends on W […] So let's clean it up in the long last !
quotes.context: In notes around Pursuing Stacks on test categories, he realises a notion he had carried for months was simpler than he thought.

quotes.text: Ce sont des genres d'animaux rencontrés naturellement par Dwork, Katz, …
quotes.en: These are the kinds of animals naturally encountered by Dwork, Katz, …
quotes.context: Notes for a lecture on Dieudonné theory, just after defining a crystal.

quotes.text: Si A s'y mettait, dans un prochain coup B […] capturerait E' — et de proche en proche il capturerait toutes les pierres de A ! […] même si A avait un avantage considérable sur B par les territoires conquis !
quotes.en: If A played there, on a next move B […] would capture E' — and step by step he would capture all of A's stones! […] even if A had a considerable advantage over B in conquered territory!
quotes.context: Pages in his hand writing out the rules of the game of go, here the end-of-game exemption from the obligation to play.

quotes.text: Étant peut-être empêché […] […] faute d'assurer un cours de 1er cycle au 1er trimestre, je vais peut-être […] faire un petit séminaire d'algèbre, et envisage de le faire sur les fourbis de Mme Sinh, éventuellement transposés dans le contexte des « champs ».
quotes.en: Being perhaps prevented […] […] for want of giving a first-cycle course in the first term, I shall perhaps […] run a small algebra seminar, and am thinking of doing it on Mrs Sinh's stuff, possibly transposed into the setting of « stacks ».
quotes.context: Opening of the 1974 letter to Deligne, planning a Montpellier seminar on Hoàng Xuân Sính's thesis on Gr-categories.

quotes.text: Question : Le triangle exact (T) et la suite exacte (*) sont-ils connus par les compétents (Quillen, Breen, Illusie…) ? Connaissent-ils des variantes « supérieures » ?
quotes.en: Question: are the exact triangle (T) and the exact sequence (*) known to the competent ones (Quillen, Breen, Illusie…)? Do they know « higher » variants?
quotes.context: Closing question of a letter to Deligne, Lodève, 27 August 1974, on Picard stacks, which Deligne forwarded to Breen.

quotes.text: (Enfin, bien sûr faisceautiser et relativiser… !!!)
quotes.en: (And finally, of course, sheafify and relativise… !!!)
quotes.context: End of a programme for recovering a homotopy type from a de Rham–type complex with divided powers.

quotes.text: Je m'aperçois finalement que j'ai pas mal bafouillé pour arriver : trouver les formulations simples — car j'ai mélangé des propriétés purement ensemblistes de l'ens. ordonné […], ses interprétations semi-simpliciales et les aspects topologiques. Je reprends
quotes.en: I realise at last that I have stammered quite a bit in getting to the simple formulations — because I mixed up purely set-theoretic properties of the ordered set […], its semi-simplicial interpretations and the topological aspects. I start again
quotes.context: Notes on unfolding stratified spaces, where he breaks off a tangled construction to start it afresh.

quotes.text: […] un magnifique succès ! Sans aller plus loin dans les vérifications, c'est un […] que l'intuition qu'il y a une théorie des […] de types d'homotopie […], est bien correcte.
quotes.en: […] a magnificent success! Without going further into the checks, it is a […] that the intuition that there is a theory of […] of homotopy types […] is indeed correct.
quotes.context: Recovering the cohomology of the sphere from a gluing of pieces, taken as evidence for a van Kampen theorem for homotopy types.

quotes.text: Il me semble d'ailleurs, réflexion faite, que cette théorie « d'intégration » des types d'homotopie, que naguère je voyais comme un lien au grand yoga des relations entre structures homotopiques (ou catégories, sur un topos disons) et les […] groupoïdes, est en fait relativement triviale, et justiciable sans doute de techniques d'explicitation des plus standard.
quotes.en: It seems to me moreover, on reflection, that this theory of « integration » of homotopy types, which I once saw as a link to the great yoga of the relations between homotopical structures (or categories, over a topos say) and […] groupoids, is in fact relatively trivial, and no doubt amenable to the most standard techniques of making things explicit.
quotes.context: Notes on stratified topoi, reassessing an idea he had once taken for a deep link.

quotes.text: À vrai dire, je vois maintenant que ces fameuses pierres telles quelles sont des côtés mal taillées — elles sont trop générales […]
quotes.en: To tell the truth, I now see that these famous stones as they stand are badly cut on some sides — they are too general […]
quotes.context: He had chosen certain pieces as the building « stones » of a stratified space and now finds them ill-suited.

quotes.text: […] Il y a un pt qui en ce moment m'échappe. Je ne suis plus trop dans le coup, et devrait reconsulter des notes des semaines précédentes.
quotes.en: […] There is a point that escapes me at the moment. I am no longer really in the swing of it, and should look again at the notes of the previous weeks.
quotes.context: A circled marginal remark in the 1983 notes on arrangements of pseudo-lines, puzzled why a local system fails to exist on one of his surfaces.

quotes.text: Pendant ces deux dernières semaines, c'est […] cette opération de recollage que j'ai […]. […] je croyais avoir interprété contradictoirement la construction de recollement de 1°), mais je m'étais mélangé les pinceaux deux fois, il me semble
quotes.en: Over these last two weeks it is […] this gluing operation that I have […]. […] I thought I had interpreted the gluing construction of 1°) inconsistently, but I had got myself muddled twice over, it seems to me
quotes.context: Looking back over two weeks of work on gluing cells into a surface built from pseudo-line arrangements.

quotes.text: c'était un cas que je crois avoir un peu vite j'avais écarté (c'était vraiment un bâton-dans-les-roues, rétrospectivement !).
quotes.en: it was a case that I believe I had dismissed a little too quickly (it was really a spoke in the wheel, in retrospect!).
quotes.context: Reviewing which of four gluing conventions he had wrongly rejected earlier.

quotes.text: Je viens de vérifier, sauf erreur (j'ai fait […] une d'erreurs encore dans le cours de la vérification !) que les trois possibilités […] donnent lieu aux bons circuits autour d'une position supersingulière, il n'y a que B2 que dérange complètement (or il semblerait que c'était sur B2 que je m'étais arrêté pendant une paire de semaines, Dieu sait pourquoi !).
quotes.en: I have just checked, barring error (I made […] more errors again in the course of the checking!) that the three possibilities […] give the right circuits around a supersingular position; only B2 upsets everything (and it would seem that it was on B2 that I had stopped for a couple of weeks, God knows why!).
quotes.context: Checking four candidate conventions for gluing, and finding that the one he had settled on for weeks was the only bad one.

quotes.text: Mais les circuits plus généraux restent mystérieux pour moi — je ne sais s'ils sont valables !
quotes.en: But the more general circuits remain mysterious to me — I do not know whether they are valid!
quotes.context: Notes on circuits in a cell complex built from pseudo-line arrangements.

quotes.text: Hélas on ne trouve pas les bons circuits supersinguliers — ce n'est pas l'aboutissement, si alléchant que cela paraisse !
quotes.en: Alas, one does not find the right supersingular circuits — this is not the outcome, however tempting it may look!
quotes.context: A promising variant of his gluing construction turns out to fail a test he had set for it.

quotes.text: J'ai commencé à faire l'exercice, mais j'ai l'impression que je n'ai pas la peine de l'expliciter jusqu'au bout. Ça doit avoir été fait depuis longtemps (Hilbert ?) dans le cas totalement ordonné (et divisible) […]
quotes.en: I began doing the exercise, but I have the feeling that it is not worth my while to spell it out to the end. It must have been done long ago (Hilbert?) in the totally ordered (and divisible) case […]
quotes.context: Characterising an ordered interval by a betweenness relation, in his axiomatics of « networks » of places.

quotes.text: (gener.) « topology » = study of topoi. (Why it is a natural and useful generalisation of the notion of topological space? a) It is the natural setting for most « algebraic » (and non algebraic) structures. b) As such, it allows to construct classifying topoi for such structures (possibly all): algebra = topology!
quotes.context: Lecture notes introducing the notion of a topos and arguing for it.

quotes.text: NB Tous les schémas envisagés par les Anciens étaient de t.f. et séparés sur des corps. La plupart des schémas qu'on envisage couramment on pourrait les supposer séparés ; pratiquement tous ceux qu'on rencontre sont quasi-séparés. Beaucoup sont qu.-cpts — mais il y en a d'importants qui ne le sont pas.
quotes.en: NB All the schemes considered by the Ancients were of finite type and separated over fields. Most of the schemes one commonly considers could be assumed separated; practically all those one meets are quasi-separated. Many are quasi-compact — but there are important ones that are not.
quotes.context: Course outline on the general properties of schemes and morphisms.

quotes.text: A.G. is a messy subject, even more foundations, we cannot give anything like a detailed exposition of all of it in our summer course. We will have to give rather a survey of some key points, being rather sketchy for proofs — most of which are straightforward.
quotes.context: Prerequisites page of a summer course on algebraic geometry and algebraic groups.
